title: Geo Ong rides helicopter from Ilocos Sur to QC after LTO suspends license
summary: With his driver's license suspended for 90 days after he posted a motorcycle ride that showed him without a helmet, social media personality Geo Ong on Monday rode a helicopter from Ilocos Sur to…

blocks.text: With his driver's license suspended for 90 days after he posted a motorcycle ride that showed him without a helmet, social media personality Geo Ong on Monday rode a helicopter from Ilocos Sur to Quezon City en route to the Land Transportation Office.
According to Oscar Oida's report on "24 Oras," Ong was driven in a luxury car to the LTO, where he was met by fans.
He had posted about his helicopter ride and plan to be at the LTO on Monday. He deleted his posts, but still followers came to the agency in droves.
The visit also coincided with a protest staged by transport group MANIBELA.

LTO chief Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao expressed displeasure over Ong’s announcement and manner of going to the agency’s Quezon City office, saying the visit appeared to have been turned into a fan meet and an opportunity to create social media content.
Lacanilao said Ong had initially requested a meeting with him, even though it was not part of the influencer’s scheduled appearance before the agency.
The LTO chief also stressed that influencers should be mindful of the example they set for their followers, particularly children who may imitate their actions.
He added that popular personalities, especially those who can afford to travel comfortably, should set a good example instead of flaunting their wealth when visiting government offices.
Ong, for his part, admitted that riding a motorcycle without a helmet was wrong.
“We are only human, and sometimes we make mistakes. Not everything we do should be imitated. Sometimes, we learn from our mistakes, and that is why we can tell you what you should do,” he said.
However, Ong saw nothing wrong with taking a helicopter to Quezon City, explaining that it was their available means of transportation.
Ong surrendered his driver’s license on Monday in compliance with the 90-day preventive suspension imposed by the LTO. –NB, GMA News
